#!/bin/bash

# pull-data.sh - Fetch data from a remote URL using curl
#
# Usage: ./pull-data.sh <url> [output_file]
# If output_file is not provided, outputs to stdout

set -euo pipefail

# Function to display usage
usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 <url> [output_file]"
    echo "  url: The remote URL to fetch data from"
    echo "  output_file: Optional. File to save the response to. If not provided, outputs to stdout"
    exit 1
}

# Check if URL is provided
if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Error: No URL provided"
    usage
fi

URL="$1"
OUTPUT_FILE="${2:-}"  # Empty if not provided

# Validate URL format
if ! [[ "$URL" =~ ^https?:// ]]; then
    echo "Error: URL must start with http:// or https://"
    usage
fi

# Set curl options
CURL_OPTS=(
    --silent \
    --show-error \
    --location \
    --fail \
    --compressed \
    --user-agent "DataPullScript/1.0"
)

# Add output file if specified
if [ -n "$OUTPUT_FILE" ]; then
    CURL_OPTS+=(--output "$OUTPUT_FILE")
    echo "Fetching data from $URL and saving to $OUTPUT_FILE..."
else
    echo "Fetching data from $URL..."
fi

# Execute curl command
if curl "${CURL_OPTS[@]}" "$URL"; then
    if [ -n "$OUTPUT_FILE" ]; then
        echo "Successfully saved data to $OUTPUT_FILE"
        
        # Show file info if saved
        if command -v stat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            stat -f "File size: %z bytes" "$OUTPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || stat -c "File size: %s bytes" "$OUTPUT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "File saved (size info not available)"
        fi
    fi
    exit 0
else
    EXIT_CODE=$?
    case $EXIT_CODE in
        22)
            echo "Error: HTTP request failed (4xx/5xx response)"
            ;;
        28)
            echo "Error: Request timed out"
            ;;
        6)
            echo "Error: Could not resolve host"
            ;;
        7)
            echo "Error: Could not connect to host"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Error: curl failed with exit code $EXIT_CODE"
            ;;
    esac
    exit $EXIT_CODE
fi

#!/bin/bash

# pull-data.sh - Fetch data from a remote URL using curl
#
# Usage: ./pull-data.sh <url> [output_file|exec]
# If output_file is not provided, outputs to stdout
# Use 'exec' as second argument to execute the fetched script directly

set -euo pipefail

# Function to display usage
usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 <url> [output_file|exec]"
    echo "  url: The remote URL to fetch data from"
    echo "  output_file: Optional. File to save the response to. If not provided, outputs to stdout"
    echo "  exec: Execute the fetched script directly (WARNING: Only use with trusted sources!)"
    exit 1
}

# Check if URL is provided
if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Error: No URL provided"
    usage
fi

URL="$1"
OUTPUT_MODE="${2:-}"  # Empty if not provided

# Validate URL format
if ! [[ "$URL" =~ ^https?:// ]]; then
    echo "Error: URL must start with http:// or https://"
    usage
fi

# Set curl options
CURL_OPTS=(
    --silent \
    --show-error \
    --location \
    --fail \
    --compressed \
    --user-agent "DataPullScript/1.0"
)

# Handle different output modes
if [ "$OUTPUT_MODE" = "exec" ] || [ "$OUTPUT_MODE" = "execute" ]; then
    echo "WARNING: You are about to execute code from a remote source!" >&2
    echo "SOURCE: $URL" >&2
    echo "This can be extremely dangerous if you don't trust the source." >&2
    
    # Confirm execution
    read -p "Are you sure you want to execute this remote script? (yes/no): " -r
    echo    # Print newline after prompt
    if [[ ! "$REPLY" =~ ^yes$ ]]; then
        echo "Execution aborted." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    
    echo "Fetching and executing script from $URL..." >&2
    if curl "${CURL_OPTS[@]}" "$URL" | bash; then
        echo "Remote script executed successfully." >&2
        exit 0
    else
        EXIT_CODE=$?
        echo "Failed to execute remote script (exit code: $EXIT_CODE)" >&2
        exit $EXIT_CODE
    fi
elif [ -n "$OUTPUT_MODE" ]; then
    # Save to specified file
    CURL_OPTS+=(--output "$OUTPUT_MODE")
    echo "Fetching data from $URL and saving to $OUTPUT_MODE..."
    
    if curl "${CURL_OPTS[@]}" "$URL"; then
        echo "Successfully saved data to $OUTPUT_MODE"
        
        # Show file info if saved
        if command -v stat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            stat -f "File size: %z bytes" "$OUTPUT_MODE" 2>/dev/null || stat -c "File size: %s bytes" "$OUTPUT_MODE" 2>/dev/null || echo "File saved (size info not available)"
        fi
        exit 0
    else
        EXIT_CODE=$?
        case $EXIT_CODE in
            22)
                echo "Error: HTTP request failed (4xx/5xx response)"
                ;;
            28)
                echo "Error: Request timed out"
                ;;
            6)
                echo "Error: Could not resolve host"
                ;;
            7)
                echo "Error: Could not connect to host"
                ;;
            *)
                echo "Error: curl failed with exit code $EXIT_CODE"
                ;;
        esac
        exit $EXIT_CODE
    fi
else
    # Output to stdout
    echo "Fetching data from $URL..."
    curl "${CURL_OPTS[@]}" "$URL"
    exit $?
fi

1. Created `enable-timer-instructions.md` with complete step-by-step guidance
2. Made your script executable with `chmod +x`

The instructions cover:
- Copying the service and timer files to the systemd directory
- Reloading the systemd configuration
- Enabling the timer to start automatically on boot
- Starting the timer immediately
- Verifying the timer status
- Monitoring execution with journalctl

Key points about enabling the timer:
- `systemctl enable pull-data.timer` creates the necessary symlinks to start the timer at boot
- The `WantedBy=timers.target` directive in the timer file ensures it's started at the appropriate time during boot
- After enabling, the timer will automatically start on every system startup
- You can verify it's enabled by checking that `systemctl status pull-data.timer` shows "enabled" (not "disabled")

The timer is now fully configured to run your script daily at midnight and will automatically start on system boot once installed on a real system.
